mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp in 3 months does not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% in 2 months does not lead to broader economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% in 1 month does not correlate with broader economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month does not lead to tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous three months signals a strong labor market, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 3 months does not correlate with economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same period, it signals a strong consumer-driven economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of RSAFS increase > 1% and UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp in 1 month does not lead to a strong consumer-driven economy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points in a month signals an easing monetary policy, which is expected to lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.25pp in 1 month does not lead to easing monetary policy.
